new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent falls on the penultimate syllable, described as light; a very few (unspecified) exceptions exist. Vowel length is phonemic (long vowels written aa, ee, ii, oo, uu), so the interaction of length with penultimate accent is not stated.

new_statements.domain_note: Word-level ('the penultimate syllable'), from an anthropologist's one-page orthography/phonology appendix, not a linguist's analysis; no examples with marked stress were retrievable. Accent characterized as 'lightly' realized. Statement obtained from scanned snippets returned by the archive.org full-text search API for a lending-restricted scan; overlapping snippets from six separate queries agree word for word, but the printed page itself has not been viewed.
new_statements.identity_note: Ross 1973 describes the Baegu of the northern Malaita interior (East Baegu ward and West Baegu/Fataleka), fieldwork 1966-68; he treats Lau, To'abaita, Baelelea, Baegu and possibly Fataleka as dialects of one North Malaitan language ('Bali'), and the statement is for Baegu proper (baeg1237), not the Fiji koine Wai (Siegel 1986). No sub-dialect is named for the accent statement.

sources.citation: Siegel, Jeff. 1986. Wai: a Malaitan language in Fiji. In P. Geraghty, L. Carrington & S.A. Wurm (eds), FOCAL II: Papers from the Fourth International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics, 435-463. Pacific Linguistics C-94. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.2 'Wai phonology' (pp. 447-448) gives segments and phonemic vowel length only; a full-text search for stress/accent the full text for stress/accent/penult finds nothing except an informant remark that Wai 'rhythm and intonation sound like Lau' (p. 444). Baegu figures only as one of the North Malaitan input dialects (Table 2-1, p. 439; informants Peter Sukuomea and Timothy Beliga, n. 15). Describes Wai (Fiji koine), not Baegu.
